discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution (BB84) and entanglement-based quantum key distribution

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) found that the no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance in quantum mechanics make provably secure key distribution possible. Their security rests on physical law, not on computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) linked cryptographic security directly to entanglement and Bell-inequality violation. This turned a foundational test of quantum nonlocality into a practical resource and laid the groundwork for device-independent security. Together these ideas started the field of quantum communication. They created a new experimental frontier, first in fibre networks over hundreds of kilometres, then in satellite-to-ground links spanning more than a thousand kilometres, and now in emerging quantum networks worldwide. Bennett and Brassard also co-invented quantum teleportation (1993), another key protocol of quantum information science. Few conceptual contributions in physics have moved so directly from the foundations of quantum mechanics to a global technology.
